file.reasoning: Tests exercise a synthetic observability-stack detector that mirrors the real-world risk: a project with no APM or error-tracking dependencies cannot correlate production issues with code changes, and the tests assert both the failure mode (bare deps produce warnings) and the safe fix (Sentry + OpenTelemetry suppress all warnings).

Tests demonstrate that omitting analytics instrumentation leaves event arrays empty (foot-gun) while a PostHog-style capture wrapper correctly records the five key lifecycle events—signup, activation, first-value-moment, retention, and churn-signal—with their associated properties.

Tests verify that an unprotected auth handler allows unlimited brute-force attempts (foot-gun), while the safe implementation enforces per-IP rate limiting (429 after 5 attempts), account locking (423 after 10 failures), and counter reset on successful login.
